game.name: Convoy
game.short_description: Convoy is a tactical roguelike-like inspired by Mad Max and FTL in which you cross a wasteland in search of parts for your broken ship. Presented in pixel art and set in a future post-apocalyptic setting, Convoy is a squad based tactical combat roguelike-like in its core.

placements.verbal_evidence: I'll put it as a high C tier probably like a little between high C or or low B

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Convoy is a real-time strategy roguelike in the FTL mold, where you lead a vehicle convoy across a big world scavenging parts and items so your ship can leave the planet. He finds the genre mix unique and respects it, but the moment-to-moment play has little strategy early on and the overworld feels empty. He beat it once, found it fun, and would rather play FTL. He would revisit it once or twice since it is quick to pick up, and settles on high C, possibly edging toward low B.
praise: Real-time strategy plus roguelike structure is fairly unique and few games do it
The genre itself is distinctive and he respects the attempt
Easy to play quickly in short sessions
Unlockable starting layouts add some variety over time
Strategy becomes meaningful in the late game
criticism: Little strategy in combat; mostly click a spot and have vehicles shoot
First ~15 minutes of every run is repetitive because you always start nearly the same
Outside world is boring, lonely and empty
Exploration events and signals are not very engaging
Late-game strategy takes a long time to arrive
unique_points: Real-time convoy defence and scavenging as an FTL-style roguelike twist
Not heavy on persistent upgrades, so nothing to remember between runs and easy to drop in
design_criteria: Uniqueness: genre blend of RTS and roguelike is uncommon
Strategic depth: combat offers little decision-making early
Run pacing: slow first 15 minutes with repetition
Variety: same starting setup each run, limited by unlocks
World/exploration design: empty overworld with weak events
Meta-progression: minimal, so low memory burden and quick to play

community.one_liner: A pixel-art tactical roguelike from Convoy Games that mixes FTL's overworld of random events with real-time, Mad Max-style vehicle combat as you cross a wasteland hunting for parts to repair your ship.
community.consensus_summary: Convoy is received as a solid but flawed FTL-inspired indie. Steam users rate it Mostly Positive (about 78% of roughly 1,470 reviews), and critics land in the mixed-to-good range (Metacritic 72, OpenCritic top-critic average around 76). The concept and the vehicle-customisation loop are widely liked, but many reviewers and players say the moment-to-moment combat becomes repetitive and the difficulty can feel unfair, especially early ambushes. It was a 2015 PC release from Indietopia Games that later got console ports (PS4 at least); I found no sign of a sequel or recent major updates, and some recent Steam reviews ask for one. The developer's follow-up title Landinar: Into the Void is bundled with it on Steam.
best_things: The FTL meets Mad Max pitch is delivered faithfully; several Steam reviewers call it the only FTL-like that really feels like FTL
Upgrading and customising your vehicles and mobile base gives a strong sense of progression during a run
Random radio-signal encounters can turn into combat, text dialogue or chance-based role-play, which keeps runs varied
Tense risk/reward decisions around fuel, repairs and whether to fight, with permadeath adding stakes
Runs can be short (15 minutes) or long (2 hours), so players can tell their own hardship stories (Twinfinite)
Good replay value: extra starting vehicles unlock by completing specific tasks, and harder difficulty modes exist
Controls are easy to learn; a new player has the concepts down after a game or two (Game Informer)
A 'chill' run-after-run feel that long-time players return to years later, often pairing it with FTL
Fits its $14.99 price point; Steam reviewers call it simple but lots of fun
worst_things: Combat is the core loop and repeats so much that critics call it a slog or chore (Game Informer, Critical Hit, Gamers FTW)
Some critics say there is little real tactics beyond focus-firing and attrition, and that it lacks FTL's depth (Riot Pixels scored it 40)
Early game can feel brutally unfair: enemies outnumber you, hit hard, and ambushes appear suddenly and wipe out vehicles
Visuals and music get called threadbare, uninspired or repetitive, and the soundtrack wears out its welcome
Story and world-building are thin or annoying; narrative ambitions go unfulfilled (Games.cz)
Quality-of-life gaps and the odd bug; one mistake can ruin an entire run
Console ports suffer from controls that are too slow for commanding several vehicles and from a cluttered UI with hard-to-read fonts
improvements: More variety in encounters and enemy types so fights stop feeling like the same exchange
Deeper tactical options beyond positioning and focus fire, including more useful abilities and customisation
Smoother onboarding and a fairer early game, with better warning of or counterplay to ambushes
Quality-of-life fixes such as scrollable objective text, seeing details of unaffordable shop items, and fewer button presses in the shop on controller
Stronger story and world-building payoff, plus more polished art and audio
An update or sequel; recent positive and negative Steam reviews both ask for more support
unique_things: Real-time vehicle combat as a high-speed car chase, where you position units and use abilities, rather than FTL-style ship system management
A central mobile command vehicle that cannot move from the middle of the screen and soaks up damage each fight
Three competing factions that grow in strength over the run, forcing adaptation
A procedurally generated planet with different objectives, events and consequences each playthrough
Tactical pause plus radio-signal encounters that branch into combat, dialogue or chance-based role-play
Steam Workshop support exists, though Steam reviewers note there are very few mods
tedious_or_disliked: Fights are long and similar, so many players report the game getting boring quickly
Fuel drains most of the money early, and backtracking across the wasteland is punished
Repeated early losses: players report dying in the first ambush or first side mission and quitting
Repair costs and losing vehicles can snowball into a dead run, which players say does not respect their time
Shop and menu handling on controller takes too many button presses
divisive_points: Difficulty: some love the challenge on harder modes, others call it janky and too hard from the start (Steam threads suggest starting on Easy and getting a third vehicle early)
Depth vs repetition: some call it a satisfying roguelike and the only true FTL-like, others say it lacks tactics and depth compared with FTL
Metacritic user score is much lower (5.3 from 34 ratings) than critics (72) and Steam (Mostly Positive)
Pixel art and soundtrack are charming to some and bland or repetitive to others
community.reception_notes: Launched April 21, 2015 on PC (Windows, Mac, Linux) via Indietopia Games at $14.99. Critic reaction was mixed to positive with the recurring repetition complaint; Metacritic lists 17 critic reviews (7 positive, 9 mixed, 1 negative), while OpenCritic shows only 38% of critics recommending it despite a mid-70s average. Steam sits at Mostly Positive, and estimates suggest 200k-500k owners and roughly $599k gross revenue (Boxleiter-style estimate, treat as order-of-magnitude). It later came to consoles; PS4 reviewers liked the game but found the controller scheme clumsy and recommended the PC version. The game has Steam Workshop support. I found no evidence of ongoing development, and recent Steam reviews (as late as 2026) are still asking for an update or sequel.
